newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close up, but bidders watch strikes.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close up, but bidders watch strikes.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up slightly in light trade even as labor strife continued and foreign investors were drawn to higher returns in other regional markets, traders and analysts said.
The bolsa's leading .IBC index closed up 1.14 percent at 6,469.84 points as 22.3 million shares traded worth 4.3 billion bolivars ($9 million).

"The market's correction from the New Year run-up looks to have halted today," said one trader, who added that subsequent performance depended, however, on adroit government handling of the doctors and teachers strikes.

Venezuela has so far forestalled doctors and teachers steep wage claims, although its earlier offer of a uniform 25 percent public sector wage increase weakened Friday when it offered doctors a 65 pay percent rise.
Among traded issues, 27 rose, 11 fell and eight closed flat. Among leading stocks, Electricidad de Caracas gained 4.00 bolivars to end at 489.00 while CANTV edged up 1.00 bolivar to end at 1946.00.
Prospects for next week look slim. "Venezuela won't be much in favor while deeper Latin American markets continue to offer such good returns," said one London based analyst.
According to Morgan Stanley, Venezuelan stocks have slipped 2.7 percent this year compared to gains of seven percent and more in Brazil, Argentina and Mexico.
